evidence.claim: The bank's model scored this transaction 0.79, in its second-highest band.
The purchase was made online, without the card present.
The amount is $292.36, under the $500 band.
The amount is $292.36, not the sub-$5 size a probe authorisation uses.
Every one of the card's unnamed match flags (M1-M9) is true.
The transaction carries no distance value (an unnamed Vesta field).
The card has 35 prior purchases of product code C.
The previous transaction was 401.9 hours earlier.
The previous transaction was more than ten minutes earlier.
This card has never been charged near $292.36 before.
$292.36 is above this card's prior mean of $44.66.
$292.36 is more than two standard deviations above this card's prior mean ($95.93).
Fraud Policy R4. No reply within 24 hours — applied here because no reply within 24 hours

Fraud Policy §3a. A case is not a report — applied here because 3a: no report. exposure $292.36 is at or below $1,000; the activity connects to no shared device profile, region cluster or other customer's fraud.

case.summary: This is an online card-not-present transaction with several fraud-leaning signals: a high model score, all unnamed match flags true, no distance value, and an amount that is well above the card’s prior mean and outside its usual range. The card also has a prior confirmed card-not-present fraud case, which makes this pattern more concerning. At the same time, the amount is not a tiny probe authorization and the card has 35 prior purchases of product code C, so the evidence supports suspicious card-not-present use rather than card testing. There is not enough here to call it legitimate.
